problem_text: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

ranking.title: Patch-level positive-unlabelled learning: normal-image patches as labelled negatives, abnormal-image patches as unlabelled
ranking.family: Prior-based patch label estimation (PU, OT assignment, noisy labels)

Novelty.review: PU learning is established theory, but the search found no application to patch-level supervision of CLIP-based medical anomaly segmentation; framing normal-image patches as labelled negatives and abnormal-image patches as unlabelled is a well-differentiated perspective relative to MIL heuristics.

Feasibility.review: Requires a mixture-proportion estimate per dataset and balanced batches (MVFA trains with batch size 1), both manageable on one GPU; nnPU is a short loss function.

Clarity.review: The overall procedure is clear, but the risk expression in step 3 is left half-written and deferred to 'the standard estimator'; the prior-estimation step and balanced batching are well specified.

Impact.review: If it works, localisation becomes trainable from image labels with a principled objective that also applies to other CLIP adapters.

Validity.review: Sound formulation that matches the data structure; the main validity risk is bias in the estimated class prior for small lesions, which the prior-misspecification ablation addresses.

ranking.title: Asymmetric patch-level MIL with a SigLIP loss for mask-free segmentation adapters

Novelty.review: MIL-based weakly supervised lesion segmentation exists (e.g. FMaMIL), and treating normal-image patches as negatives is natural; the SigLIP patch loss and the cross-modality zero-shot setting give moderate novelty.

Feasibility.review: A single loss replacement in train_zero.py with standard hyper-parameters; highly feasible.

Clarity.review: Exceptionally precise: logits, normal and abnormal terms, k, weights, levels, optimiser and ablations are all specified.

Impact.review: Directly removes MVFA's dependence on masks for localisation; a clear baseline for the whole direction.

Validity.review: Sound and directly aligned with the verified seg-loss limitation; top-k selection can pick salient normal anatomy, which is acknowledged through ablations.

ranking.title: Bank-informed positive-unlabelled learning: patch-specific class priors from position-aware normal-bank distances
ranking.family: Prior-based patch label estimation (PU, OT assignment, noisy labels)

Novelty.review: Instance-dependent priors exist in PU theory, and memory banks are common, but their combination for mask-free medical segmentation was not found.

Feasibility.review: Combines position-aware banks, prior estimation and weighted nnPU; feasible but heavier engineering and more hyper-parameters (temperature, clipping, radius).

Clarity.review: The prior construction (softmax over bank distances rescaled to the dataset prior, then clipped) is described but somewhat ad hoc and not fully justified.

Impact.review: Potentially sharper localisation than single-prior PU, especially for small lesions.

Validity.review: Bank-derived priors are themselves noisy estimates; using them as instance priors can bias the risk estimator, and unbiasedness of the weighted nnPU under estimated instance priors is not argued.

ranking.title: Bank-gated asymmetric MIL: positives must be both text-abnormal and unlike any normal patch of the dataset

Novelty.review: Gating MIL positives with memory-bank evidence is a sensible combination of known components; related pixel-labelling-efficiency work exists in industrial AD.

Feasibility.review: Requires per-dataset banks and a gated loss; straightforward.

Clarity.review: Gating rule, fallback and weighting are clearly specified.

Impact.review: Likely to reduce MIL's selection of salient normal structures, improving PRO.

Validity.review: Agreement of two independent evidence sources is a well-founded way to raise positive precision.

ranking.title: Normal-bank pseudo-masks: localising anomalies in image-labelled source data by distance to that dataset's normal patches

Novelty.review: Memory-bank localisation is standard (PatchCore-style); using it offline to create pseudo-masks for training a CLIP segmentation branch from image labels is a moderately new use.

Feasibility.review: Offline feature extraction and coreset search on source datasets; very feasible.

Clarity.review: Clear procedure with thresholds defined on held-out normal images.

Impact.review: Simple, model-agnostic way to obtain dense supervision without masks.

Validity.review: Frozen-CLIP nearest-neighbour distances may not localise subtle medical lesions; the falsification threshold on pseudo-mask IoU is a good safeguard.

Novelty.review: The MIL ranking loss is well known from video anomaly detection (Sultani et al.); transferring it to image patches with cross-image batches is a moderate novelty.

Feasibility.review: Balanced batches and a hinge loss; easy to implement.

Clarity.review: Loss, regularisers and weights are clear.

Impact.review: Cross-image comparability of scores benefits both localisation and image scoring.

Validity.review: Sound transfer of a validated weakly supervised objective; also fixes the batch-size-1 limitation.

ranking.title: Optimal-transport label assignment of abnormal mass to patches under a lesion-fraction budget
ranking.family: Prior-based patch label estimation (PU, OT assignment, noisy labels)

Novelty.review: OT-based label assignment exists for point-supervised segmentation (Point2Mask) and detection, but not for distributing image-level anomaly labels over patches.

Feasibility.review: Sinkhorn on 289 patches per image is cheap.

Clarity.review: Costs, budget and schedule are specified.

Impact.review: Likely gains over PU are uncertain; the main benefit is sharper per-image labels.

Validity.review: Depends on the lesion-fraction budget and a neighbourhood cost whose weight is hand-set; risk of collapse to contiguous but wrong regions.

ranking.title: Position-aware normal-bank pseudo-masks: matching each patch only to normal patches from the same anatomical neighbourhood

Novelty.review: Using spatial position as the normality cue for brain lesions is close to Patch2Loc (AISTATS 2026) and to position-conditioned normal models such as PaDiM; the incremental novelty is low.

Feasibility.review: Offline banks per grid position are easy to build.

Clarity.review: Clear radius, coreset and threshold choices, including a rule for unaligned datasets.

Impact.review: Benefits mainly spatially aligned datasets (registered brain slices); limited for OCT, chest X-ray and histopathology.

Validity.review: Assumes spatial alignment that holds only for part of BMAD; the per-dataset radius rule is reasonable but the claim of alignment for liver CT is not verified.

ranking.title: Counterfactual patch replacement: learning where anomalies are from which patches, when replaced by normal tissue, flip the image decision

Novelty.review: Counterfactual perturbation for weakly supervised anomaly localisation appears in other domains (logs) but not for medical image patches in CLIP adapters.

Feasibility.review: Batched replacement at the scoring head is cheap.

Clarity.review: Procedure is clear, including the batching trick.

Impact.review: Causal localisation is attractive but gains are uncertain.

Validity.review: Replacing post-adapter tokens without propagating through later layers changes only the scoring head; with a mean-pooled score single-patch drops may be tiny for small lesions.

ranking.title: Noisy-label learning with small-loss selection: all abnormal-image patches as noisy positives
ranking.family: Prior-based patch label estimation (PU, OT assignment, noisy labels)

Novelty.review: Co-teaching and noise-robust training for medical segmentation exist; applying them to image-label-derived patch labels is moderately new.

Feasibility.review: Two adapter copies double training cost but remain feasible.

Clarity.review: Schedule and selection rule are clear.

Impact.review: Avoids explicit priors, but the expected gain over PU is modest.

Validity.review: The forget-rate schedule implicitly encodes the lesion fraction, so the 'no prior needed' claim is only partly true.
